title: Lesson 3 Quiz: Sustainable Consumption and Resource Allocation
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it meets the lesson's completion requirement (quiz submitted), and your score is recorded separately.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not yet reviewed by a human (admin) and not to be given to students.
Rewritten in English from the Korean draft. Not reviewed or approved by a human.

questions.prompt: When you leave part of your school cafeteria lunch uneaten, what is wasted along with it?

choices.text: The food plus the water, power, and labor used to grow, ship, and cook it
Just the food left on the tray at the end of the meal
Very little, because the price of the lunch was already paid
The part of the lunch price that matches the share left uneaten

questions.prompt: When stores give out plastic bags for free, people tend to use more bags than they need. Which statement best explains why?

choices.text: The social cost of a plastic bag is zero once it has been made.
The cost shoppers face ($0) is below the social cost, including disposal and harm.
The cost of producing each plastic bag is very high for the store.
Plastic bags are a necessity that people need for daily life.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Making one disposable takeout container costs 30 cents, and after it is used, disposal and environmental damage cost society another 45 cents (assumed values). What is the social cost of one container, in cents? (Enter a number only.)
Which statement best describes a deposit-return system for disposable cups (you get money back when you return the cup)?

choices.text: Cup prices keep rising, so the burden on consumers grows over time.
It mainly provides information, so behavior tends to change little.
Refunds raise returns and reuse, but return sites and upkeep cost money.
It removes most of the cost of producing the cups in the first place.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A reusable shopping bag costs $3, and each time you use it for shopping, you avoid a 5-cent plastic bag fee. How many times must you use the reusable bag to earn back its price? (Enter a number only.)
